## Natural history notes

A small to medium-sized bracket fungus characterized by thin, fan-shaped to semicircular caps with pale cream, tan, or “latte”-colored surfaces and a whitish pore layer underneath. In Florida, it is found on dead hardwood, fallen branches, logs, stumps, and other decaying wood in hammocks, forests, parks, yards, and other humid wooded habitats. It acts as a wood-decay fungus, helping break down dead plant material, and its tough shelf-like fruiting bodies often grow in overlapping clusters on exposed wood.
